rationale: Evidence: iteration 6 is the best design so far (937.1). Oval and s-bend finish 20/20, and slalom now finishes 20/20 (925.7), up from 11/20 at iteration 5. The remaining loss is in slalom: 0.65 line-loss events per run, rms_error 0.011, max_error 0.021, and a mean finish time of 2.92 s, close to the 3 s limit. Score sensitivity: each line-loss event costs about 15 points (120/8), and the rms term is worth about 65 points on slalom. Time is worth only about 1.6 points on slalom, so speed is a secondary lever. Iteration 6 changed mass (0.45 to 0.40) and sensor lead (y 0.05 to 0.06) together, and both moved in the right direction. Iteration 4 showed that raising kp to 6 collapses the oval and s-bend, so kp stays at 4.0. Mass is already at its 0.40 kg floor, so it cannot move further. Changes: (1) Move the sensor lead from y = 0.06 to y = 0.07 m, inside the 0.08 limit, to continue the lead trend that helped slalom. (2) Raise kd from 1.0 to 1.1 to damp the extra overshoot a larger lead can introduce. Sensor x positions, weights, kp, ki, base_speed (1.5) and line_loss (last_direction) are unchanged, so the effect is readable. Expected result: slalom line-loss events fall to about 0.4 or below and slalom rms_error drops by a few thousandths. Oval and s-bend stay near 100% completion. Steering_oscillation should stay near 0.3 or below. Hypotheses: (a) the y = 0.07 lead cuts slalom line-loss events; (b) kd 1.1 keeps oscillation at or below about 0.35; (c) completion holds at 100% on all three tracks. If slalom max_error rises or oscillation exceeds 0.35, revert to y = 0.06 and kd 1.0, which is the iteration 6 design.
